scenes.heading: Writing Dockerfiles for Data Apps
scenes.subheading: Turn your pipeline into a reproducible image
scenes.narration: A Dockerfile is a recipe that describes exactly how to build a reproducible image for your data application.

scenes.heading: Anatomy of a Dockerfile
bullets: FROM chooses a base image to build on
COPY brings your code into the image
RUN executes build steps like installing packages
CMD defines the default command to run
scenes.narration: The FROM instruction picks a base image that supplies the operating system and runtime. COPY moves your source code and dependency files into the image. RUN executes build-time commands such as installing your Python packages. And CMD declares the default command that runs when the container starts.

scenes.heading: A Dockerfile for a data job
scenes.code:
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Copy dependency file first for better layer caching
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy the rest of the source
COPY . .

CMD ["python", "run_pipeline.py"]
scenes.narration: We start from a slim Python base to keep the image small. Setting a working directory keeps paths tidy. Notice that we copy the requirements file before the rest of the code, so that the expensive install layer is cached and only rebuilt when dependencies actually change. After installing, we copy the remaining source and set the pipeline script as the default command.

scenes.text: Order instructions from least to most frequently changed so Docker reuses cached layers and builds stay fast.
scenes.narration: Each instruction creates a layer, so order them from least to most frequently changed and Docker will reuse cached layers to keep your builds fast.

scenes.heading: Fat image vs slim image
scenes.narration: A naive image starts from a full operating system and leaves build tools behind, ballooning to hundreds of megabytes. An optimized image uses a slim base and multi-stage builds to strip out anything not needed at runtime, producing a smaller and more secure result.

scenes.text: A good Dockerfile is small, cache-friendly, and pinned to specific versions for reproducible data builds.
scenes.narration: Aim for Dockerfiles that are small, cache-friendly, and pinned to specific versions so your data builds are reproducible every time.
